questions.question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant k = 2.303 x 10^-3 s^-1. Calculate time required for reactant concentration to drop from 1.0 M to 0.1 M.
Calculate the half-life period (t1/2) of a first-order reaction having rate constant k = 6.93 x 10^-4 s^-1.
For a first-order reaction, how much time is required to complete 99.9% of the reaction if its half-life t1/2 is 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: t99.9% = 10 × t1/2 = 10 × 10 minutes = 100 minutes.

questions.question: The rate of a reaction quadruples (4x) when temperature is raised from 293 K to 313 K. Calculate Activation Energy Ea. (R = 8.314 J/mol K, log 4 = 0.602)
Initial rate data for A + B -> Products: [A]=0.1, [B]=0.1, Rate=2x10^-3; [A]=0.2, [B]=0.1, Rate=4x10^-3; [A]=0.1, [B]=0.2, Rate=8x10^-3. Overall order is:
questions.explanation: Doubling [A] doubles Rate -> Order wrt A = 1. Doubling [B] quadruples Rate -> Order wrt B = 2. Overall order = 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.question: If a zero-order reaction takes 20 minutes for 50% completion, how much time will it take for 100% completion?
questions.explanation: For zero-order reactions, completion time is directly proportional to concentration change. 100% completion time = 2 × 20 = 40 minutes.

questions.question: The rate constant of a reaction is k = 2.1 x 10^10 e^(-9000/T). Calculate Activation Energy Ea in kJ/mol. (R = 8.314 J/mol K)
questions.explanation: Comparing with k = A e^(-Ea / RT), Ea / R = 9000 => Ea = 9000 × 8.314 J/mol = 74826 J/mol = 74.83 kJ/mol.

questions.question: A radioactive isotope decays with a half-life of 5730 years. What fraction of the original isotope remains after 17190 years?
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives n = 17190 / 5730 = 3. Remaining fraction = (1/2)^3 = 1/8 = 12.5%.

questions.question: For a first-order reaction A -> B, initial concentration is 0.8 M and rate is 1.6 x 10^-2 M s^-1. Calculate rate constant k.
For a reaction A + B -> Products, doubling [A] doubles rate, while doubling [B] does not change rate. Rate law expression is:
questions.explanation: Order wrt A = 1, Order wrt B = 0. Rate = k [A]^1 [B]^0 = k [A].

quiz_sets.set_name: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry - Set 71
quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on mole calculations, molar mass, stoichiometry, molarity, molality, and empirical formulas.

questions.question: Calculate the number of moles of CO2 present in 88 grams of carbon dioxide gas. (Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles = Given Mass / Molar Mass = 88 g / 44 g/mol = 2 moles.

questions.question: What is the molarity of a solution prepared by dissolving 4 g of NaOH in enough water to form 250 mL of solution? (Molar mass NaOH = 40 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 4 / 40 = 0.1 mol. Volume of solution = 250 mL = 0.25 L. Molarity = 0.1 / 0.25 = 0.4 M.

questions.question: How many water molecules are present in 36 grams of pure water?
questions.explanation: Moles of H2O = 36 g / 18 g/mol = 2 moles. Number of molecules = 2 × N_A = 2 × 6.022 × 10<sup>23</sup> = 1.204 × 10<sup>24</sup> molecules.

questions.question: What volume of oxygen gas (O2) at STP is required to completely burn 16 g of methane (CH4)?
questions.explanation: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. 1 mole of CH4 (16g) requires 2 moles of O2. At STP, 2 moles of O2 occupy 2 × 22.4 L = 44.8 L.

questions.question: Calculate the molality of a solution containing 10 g of glucose (C6H12O6, Molar mass = 180 g/mol) in 90 g of water.
questions.explanation: Moles of solute = 10 / 180 = 0.0555 mol. Mass of solvent in kg = 90 / 1000 = 0.09 kg. Molality = 0.0555 / 0.09 ≈ 0.617 m (approx 0.62 m).

questions.question: What is the mass percentage of carbon in glucose (C6H12O6)? (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of C6H12O6 = (6×12) + (12×1) + (6×16) = 72 + 12 + 96 = 180 g/mol. Mass of C = 72 g. Mass % = (72 / 180) × 100 = 40%.

questions.question: How many moles of helium gas occupy 5.6 Litres at STP?
questions.explanation: At STP, 1 mole = 22.4 L. Moles = 5.6 L / 22.4 L = 0.25 mol.

questions.question: A compound contains 50% element X (Atomic mass = 10) and 50% element Y (Atomic mass = 20) by mass. Find its empirical formula.
questions.explanation: Relative ratio: X = 50 / 10 = 5. Y = 50 / 20 = 2.5. Dividing by smallest (2.5): X = 5 / 2.5 = 2, Y = 2.5 / 2.5 = 1. Empirical formula = X2Y.

questions.question: What is the formality/normality of 0.5 M H2SO4 solution for complete neutralization?
questions.explanation: H2SO4 is a dibasic acid (n-factor = 2). Normality = Molarity × n-factor = 0.5 × 2 = 1.0 N.

questions.question: Calculate the number of atoms present in 4.25 g of NH3. (Atomic mass: N = 14, H = 1)
questions.explanation: Moles of NH3 = 4.25 / 17 = 0.25 mol. Number of molecules = 0.25 × N_A. Each NH3 has 4 atoms (1 N + 3 H). Total atoms = 4 × 0.25 × N_A = 1 × N_A = 6.022 × 10<sup>23</sup> atoms.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on first law of thermodynamics, enthalpy, entropy, Gibbs free energy, and Hess's law.

questions.question: In a process, 701 J of heat is absorbed by a system and 394 J of work is done by the system. What is the change in internal energy (ΔU)?
questions.explanation: According to 1st Law of Thermodynamics: ΔU = q + w. Here q = +701 J (absorbed), w = -394 J (done by system). ΔU = 701 - 394 = +307 J.

questions.question: For a reaction at 300 K, ΔH = -10 kcal and ΔS = -20 cal/K. Calculate ΔG and state whether the reaction is spontaneous.
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. Here ΔH = -10 kcal, ΔS = -20 cal/K = -0.02 kcal/K, T = 300 K. ΔG = -10 - (300 × -0.02) = -10 + 6 = -4 kcal. Since ΔG < 0, it is spontaneous.

questions.question: Calculate the enthalpy change (ΔH) for a reaction where 2 moles of gas expand at a constant temperature of 27°C from 10 L to 20 L against a constant pressure.
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, internal energy ΔU = 0 and enthalpy change ΔH = ΔU + Δ(PV) = 0.

questions.question: The heat of combustion of carbon to CO2 is -393.5 kJ/mol. How much heat is released upon burning 3 grams of carbon?
questions.explanation: Moles of carbon in 3g = 3 / 12 = 0.25 mol. Heat released = 0.25 × 393.5 kJ = 98.375 kJ.

questions.question: If a system absorbs 500 J of heat and its entropy increases by 1.25 J/K, at what constant temperature did this process take place?
questions.explanation: Formula: ΔS = q / T => T = q / ΔS = 500 J / 1.25 J/K = 400 K.

questions.question: Work done during reversible isothermal expansion of 1 mole of an ideal gas from 1 L to 10 L at 300 K is: (R = 8.314 J/K·mol, ln 10 = 2.303)
If C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g), ΔH = -393.5 kJ and CO(g) + 0.5 O2(g) -> CO2(g), ΔH = -283.0 kJ, calculate heat of formation of CO(g).
questions.explanation: Target rxn: C + 0.5 O2 -> CO. Subtract equation (2) from (1): ΔHf(CO) = -393.5 - (-283.0) = -393.5 + 283.0 = -110.5 kJ.

questions.question: Enthalpy of neutralization of strong acid with strong base is -57.1 kJ/mol. How much heat is evolved when 0.5 mole of HCl is neutralized by 0.5 mole of NaOH?
questions.explanation: Heat evolved for 1 mole = 57.1 kJ. For 0.5 mole = 0.5 × 57.1 = 28.55 kJ.

questions.question: Calculate the temperature at which a reaction becomes spontaneous if ΔH = +30 kJ/mol and ΔS = +60 J/K·mol.
questions.explanation: For spontaneity ΔG = ΔH - T ΔS < 0 => T > ΔH / ΔS = (30,000 J/mol) / (60 J/K·mol) = 500 K. So reaction becomes spontaneous above 500 K.

questions.question: Specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J/g·°C. Calculate heat required to raise temperature of 100 g of water from 20°C to 50°C.
questions.explanation: q = m × c × ΔT = 100 g × 4.18 J/g·°C × (50 - 20)°C = 418 × 30 = 12540 J.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on Raoult's law, elevation in boiling point, depression in freezing point, and osmotic pressure.

questions.question: The vapour pressure of pure benzene at a certain temperature is 0.850 bar. A non-volatile solute of mass 0.5 g added to 39 g of benzene (molar mass 78 g/mol) lowers vapour pressure to 0.845 bar. What is the molar mass of the solute?
Calculate the osmotic pressure of a 5% (w/v) solution of cane sugar (molar mass = 342 g/mol) at 15°C. (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K)
questions.explanation: 5% w/v = 5g in 100 mL = 50 g/L. Concentration C = 50 / 342 = 0.146 mol/L. T = 15 + 273 = 288 K. Osmotic Pressure π = C × R × T = 0.146 × 0.0821 × 288 ≈ 3.46 atm.

questions.question: Boiling point of water is 100°C. What will be the boiling point of a solution containing 6 g of urea (Molar mass = 60) in 200 g of water? (Kb for water = 0.52 K kg/mol)
What is the van 't Hoff factor (i) for a completely dissociated aqueous solution of K2SO4?
questions.explanation: K2SO4 dissociates as: K2SO4 -> 2 K⁺ + SO4²⁻ (total 3 ions). For 100% dissociation i = n = 3.

questions.question: The freezing point depression constant (Kf) for benzene is 5.12 K kg/mol. A 0.2 m solution of a non-electrolyte in benzene will freeze at what temperature below pure benzene?
questions.explanation: ΔTf = Kf × m = 5.12 × 0.2 = 1.024 K.

questions.question: A solution contains 1 mole of liquid A (P0_A = 100 mm Hg) and 3 moles of liquid B (P0_B = 200 mm Hg). What is total vapour pressure of ideal solution?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction XA = 1/4 = 0.25, XB = 3/4 = 0.75. P_total = XA × P0_A + XB × P0_B = (0.25 × 100) + (0.75 × 200) = 25 + 150 = 175 mm Hg.

questions.question: 0.1 M NaCl solution has higher boiling point elevation than 0.1 M glucose solution because van 't Hoff factor for NaCl is:
questions.explanation: NaCl dissociates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ (i = 2), whereas glucose does not dissociate (i = 1). ΔTb is proportional to i.

questions.question: What is the mole fraction of solute in a 1 molal aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: 1 molal solution has 1 mole solute in 1000 g water. Moles of water = 1000 / 18 = 55.55. X_solute = 1 / (1 + 55.55) = 1 / 56.55 ≈ 0.0177.

questions.question: Henry's law constant for CO2 in water is 1.67 × 10<sup>8</sup> Pa at 298 K. Calculate mole fraction of CO2 in water at 2.5 atm (1 atm = 101325 Pa) pressure.
Isotonic solutions must have the same:
questions.explanation: By definition, isotonic solutions have equal osmotic pressure at a given temperature.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on Nernst equation, molar conductivity, Faraday's laws, rate laws, and reaction half-life.

questions.question: The half-life period of a first-order reaction is 60 minutes. What is the rate constant (k) of the reaction?
questions.explanation: For 1st order reaction: k = 0.693 / t1/2 = 0.693 / 60 = 0.01155 min<sup>-1</sup>.

questions.question: How much electricity in Coulombs is required to reduce 1 mole of Cr2O7²⁻ to Cr³⁺ in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: Cr2O7²⁻ + 14 H⁺ + 6 e⁻ -> 2 Cr³⁺ + 7 H2O. 1 mole of Cr2O7²⁻ requires 6 moles of electrons = 6 Faraday = 6 × 96500 = 579,000 C.

questions.question: The cell potential (E°cell) of the reaction Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) -> Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) is 1.10 V. Calculate standard Gibbs free energy change (ΔG°) for the reaction. (F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: ΔG° = -n F E°cell. Here n = 2 electrons. ΔG° = -2 × 96500 × 1.10 = -212,300 J/mol = -212.3 kJ/mol.

questions.question: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 32 minutes. How much time will it take to complete 50% of the reaction?
questions.explanation: For 1st order reaction, t75% = 2 × t50%. Given t75% = 32 mins => t50% = 32 / 2 = 16 minutes.

questions.question: Resistance of a conductivity cell filled with 0.1 M KCl solution is 100 Ω. If cell constant is 1.25 cm<sup>-1</sup>, calculate the molar conductivity (Λm) of the solution.
questions.explanation: Conductivity κ = cell constant / R = 1.25 / 100 = 0.0125 S cm<sup>-1</sup>. Molar conductivity Λm = (κ × 1000) / M = (0.0125 × 1000) / 0.1 = 12.5 / 0.1 = 125 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>.

questions.question: The rate constant of a reaction is k = 2.0 × 10<sup>-3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>. What is the overall order of the reaction?
questions.explanation: Unit of k is s<sup>-1</sup>, which corresponds uniquely to a First-order reaction.

questions.question: For a zero-order reaction A -> Products, if initial concentration is [A]0 = 0.1 M and rate constant k = 0.002 M/s, what is the half-life period?
questions.explanation: For zero-order reaction: t1/2 = [A]0 / (2 k) = 0.1 / (2 × 0.002) = 0.1 / 0.004 = 25 seconds.

questions.question: A current of 1.5 A is passed through a solution of CuSO4 for 10 minutes. Calculate mass of copper deposited at cathode. (Atomic mass Cu = 63.5, 1 F = 96500 C)
questions.explanation: Q = I × t = 1.5 A × 600 s = 900 C. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ -> Cu. Mass m = (M × Q)/(n × F) = (63.5 × 900)/(2 × 96500) = 57150 / 193000 ≈ 0.296 g.

questions.question: If rate of reaction doubles when temperature increases from 300 K to 310 K, calculate Activation Energy (Ea). (R = 8.314 J/K·mol, ln 2 = 0.693)
In a galvanic cell, E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = -0.44 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. What is the standard EMF of the cell?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) - E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = 0.34 - (-0.44) = 0.34 + 0.44 = 0.78 V.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on Bohr's radius, energy levels, Rydberg formula, Heisenberg uncertainty, and quantum numbers.

questions.question: Calculate the wavelength of a photon emitted when an electron in a Hydrogen atom transitions from n = 2 to n = 1 level. (Rydberg constant R = 1.097 × 10<sup>7</sup> m<sup>-1</sup>)
What is the energy of an electron in the first excited state (n = 2) of a Hydrogen atom?
Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a ball of mass 0.1 kg moving with a velocity of 10 m/s. (h = 6.63 × 10<sup>-34</sup> J·s)
questions.explanation: λ = h / (m × v) = (6.63 × 10<sup>-34</sup>) / (0.1 × 10) = 6.63 × 10<sup>-34</sup> m.

questions.question: If uncertainty in position of an electron is 0.1 nm, calculate the minimum uncertainty in its momentum (Δp). (h/4π = 5.27 × 10<sup>-35</sup> J·s)
questions.explanation: Δx × Δp ≥ h / 4π => Δp ≥ (5.27 × 10<sup>-35</sup>) / (10<sup>-10</sup> m) = 5.27 × 10<sup>-25</sup> kg·m/s.

questions.question: How many nodal planes (angular nodes) are present in a 3d orbital?
questions.explanation: Number of angular nodes / nodal planes = azimuthal quantum number l. For d orbital l = 2.

questions.question: Calculate the radius of the first orbit (n = 1) of He⁺ ion. (Radius of 1st orbit of H = 0.529 Å)
What is the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a subshell with l = 3 (f-subshell)?
questions.explanation: Max electrons = 2 (2l + 1). For l = 3: 2 × (2×3 + 1) = 2 × 7 = 14 electrons.

questions.question: Calculate frequency of radiation emitted when electron falls from n = 4 to n = 1 in H-atom. (E1 = -13.6 eV, E4 = -0.85 eV, h = 4.14 × 10<sup>-15</sup> eV·s)
Find the total number of orbitals associated with principal quantum number n = 3.
questions.explanation: Total number of orbitals in a shell = n<sup>2</sup>. For n = 3: 3<sup>2</sup> = 9 orbitals (1s-like + 3p + 5d).

questions.question: Ratio of magnetic moments of Fe²⁺ (d⁶) and Fe³⁺ (d⁵) ions is:
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ (d⁶) has 4 unpaired e⁻ => μ = √(4×6) = √24 BM. Fe³⁺ (d⁵) has 5 unpaired e⁻ => μ = √(5×7) = √35 BM. Ratio = √24 : √35.

questions.question: A vessel contains 3.2 g of methane (CH4) and 4.4 g of CO2. Find total pressure if volume is 10 L at 27°C. (R = 0.0821 L·atm/K·mol)
questions.explanation: Moles CH4 = 3.2 / 16 = 0.2 mol. Moles CO2 = 4.4 / 44 = 0.1 mol. Total moles n = 0.3. P = n R T / V = 0.3 × 0.0821 × 300 / 10 = 0.7389 atm.

questions.question: Ratio of rate of diffusion of Hydrogen gas (H2) to Oxygen gas (O2) at same T and P is:
A gas occupies 500 mL at 27°C and 760 mm Hg. What will be its volume at 127°C at constant pressure?
Density of a gas is 1.43 g/L at STP. Calculate molar mass of the gas.
questions.explanation: At STP 1 mole = 22.4 L. Molar mass M = density × 22.4 L = 1.43 × 22.4 ≈ 32.0 g/mol (Oxygen).

questions.question: In van der Waals equation (P + a/V<sup>2</sup>)(V - b) = RT, the unit of van der Waals constant 'a' is:
questions.explanation: Pressure correction term a / V<sup>2</sup> has units of Pressure. So a = P × V<sup>2</sup> / n<sup>2</sup> = atm L<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-2</sup>.

questions.question: Boyle's temperature (T_B) of a gas in terms of van der Waals constants a and b is given by:
questions.explanation: By definition, Boyle's temperature T_B = a / (R × b).

questions.question: Critical temperature (T_c) of a gas is given by formula:
questions.explanation: Critical temperature T_c = 8a / (27 R b).

questions.question: Compressibility factor Z = PV / nRT for an ideal gas is equal to:
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas, PV = nRT, hence Z = 1 under all conditions of T and P.

questions.question: Average kinetic energy of 0.5 mole of N2 gas at 300 K is: (R = 8.314 J/K·mol)
questions.explanation: E = (3/2) × n R T = 1.5 × 0.5 × 8.314 × 300 ≈ 1870.6 J.

questions.question: 50 mL of a gas diffuses through a porous membrane in 20 seconds. Under identical conditions, 40 mL of gas X diffuses in 30 seconds. Find molecular mass of X if mass of first gas is 16.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on Kp, Kc, Le Chatelier's principle, pH calculations, solubility product (Ksp), and buffer solutions.

questions.question: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g), Kp = 0.5 atm<sup>-2</sup> at 400 K. Find Kc. (R = 0.0821 L·atm/K·mol)
questions.explanation: Δng = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2. Kp = Kc (RT)<sup>Δng</sup> => Kc = Kp × (RT)<sup>2</sup> = 0.5 × (0.0821 × 400)<sup>2</sup> = 0.5 × (32.84)<sup>2</sup> ≈ 539.2 M<sup>-2</sup>.

questions.question: Calculate the pH of a 10<sup>-3</sup> M solution of HCl at 25°C.
questions.explanation: pH = -log[H⁺] = -log(10<sup>-3</sup>) = 3.

questions.question: Calculate pH of 0.005 M H2SO4 solution assuming complete ionization.
If solubility of AgCl in water is 1 × 10<sup>-5</sup> mol/L, calculate its solubility product Ksp.
questions.explanation: AgCl <=> Ag⁺ + Cl⁻. Ksp = s × s = s<sup>2</sup> = (10<sup>-5</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 1 × 10<sup>-10</sup>.

questions.question: Calculate pH of a buffer solution containing 0.1 M CH3COOH and 0.1 M CH3COONa. (pKa of CH3COOH = 4.74)
questions.explanation: By Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]) = 4.74 + log(0.1/0.1) = 4.74 + 0 = 4.74.

questions.question: Solubility product of BaSO4 is Ksp = 1.1 × 10<sup>-10</sup>. Calculate its molar solubility in pure water.
questions.explanation: BaSO4 <=> Ba²⁺ + SO4²⁻. Ksp = s<sup>2</sup> => s = √(Ksp) = √(1.1 × 10<sup>-10</sup>) ≈ 1.048 × 10<sup>-5</sup> M.

questions.question: If dissociation constant of weak acid HA is Ka = 10<sup>-5</sup>, find degree of dissociation α in 0.1 M solution.
questions.explanation: By Ostwald's Dilution Law: α = √(Ka / C) = √(10<sup>-5</sup> / 0.1) = √(10<sup>-4</sup>) = 10<sup>-2</sup> = 0.01.

questions.question: What is the pH of a 10<sup>-8</sup> M HCl solution in water at 25°C?
questions.explanation: Water ionization contributes [H⁺]_water = 10<sup>-7</sup> M. Total [H⁺] = 10<sup>-7</sup> + 10<sup>-8</sup> = 1.1 × 10<sup>-7</sup> M. pH = -log(1.1 × 10<sup>-7</sup>) ≈ 6.96 to 6.98.

questions.question: Equilibrium constant for N2 + O2 <=> 2NO is K. What is equilibrium constant for 0.5 N2 + 0.5 O2 <=> NO?
questions.explanation: Multiplying chemical equation by 0.5 raises its equilibrium constant to the power 0.5, i.e., √K.

questions.question: Calculate pOH of a solution whose pH is 9.25 at 25°C.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on oxidation numbers, equivalent weights, n-factor, volumetric titration, and redox stoichiometry.

questions.question: What is the oxidation state of Chromium in Potassium Dichromate (K2Cr2O7)?
Equivalent weight of KMnO4 in acidic medium is: (Molar mass of KMnO4 = M)
questions.explanation: In acidic medium MnO4⁻ + 5e⁻ -> Mn²⁺. n-factor = 5. Equivalent weight = M / 5.

questions.question: What volume of 0.1 N KMnO4 is required to completely oxidize 20 mL of 0.2 N FeSO4 solution?
questions.explanation: By law of equivalence: N1 × V1 = N2 × V2 => 0.1 × V1 = 0.2 × 20 => 0.1 V1 = 4 => V1 = 40 mL.

questions.question: What is the oxidation number of Sulfur in Sodium Thiosulfate (Na2S2O3)?
Equivalent mass of oxalic acid (H2C2O4·2H2O, Molar mass = 126 g/mol) is:
questions.explanation: Oxalic acid is a dibasic acid (n-factor = 2). Equivalent mass = 126 / 2 = 63 g/equiv.

questions.question: Number of moles of electrons required to reduce 1 mole of MnO4⁻ to MnO2 in neutral/faintly alkaline medium is:
questions.explanation: MnO4⁻ (+7) + 3e⁻ -> MnO2 (+4). Number of electrons required = 3.

questions.question: In the reaction H2S + Cl2 -> 2 HCl + S, which substance acts as reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Sulfur in H2S is oxidized from -2 to 0. Hence H2S acts as reducing agent.

questions.question: Mass of K2Cr2O7 (Molar mass = 294 g/mol) required to prepare 500 mL of 0.1 N solution in acidic medium is:
questions.explanation: Eq. mass = 294 / 6 = 49. Mass = N × Eq.mass × V(L) = 0.1 × 49 × 0.5 = 2.45 g.

questions.question: Oxidation state of Phosphorus in H3PO4 (Phosphoric acid) is:
Volume of 0.5 M H2SO4 required to completely neutralize 50 mL of 1 M NaOH solution is:
questions.explanation: N1 = 0.5 × 2 = 1.0 N H2SO4. N2 = 1.0 N NaOH. N1 V1 = N2 V2 => 1.0 × V1 = 1.0 × 50 => V1 = 50 mL.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on crystal lattice, edge length, density of unit cell, packing fraction, and radius ratio.

questions.question: A element crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (fcc) lattice with edge length a = 400 pm. Calculate atomic radius r.
questions.explanation: For FCC lattice: 4 r = √2 a => r = (√2 × 400) / 4 = (1.414 × 400) / 4 = 141.4 pm.

questions.question: Number of atoms per unit cell in a Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) crystal lattice is:
questions.explanation: BCC unit cell contains 8 corner atoms × (1/8) + 1 body center atom = 1 + 1 = 2 atoms.

questions.question: Calculate density of NaCl crystal if edge length is 564 pm. (Molar mass NaCl = 58.5 g/mol, Z = 4 for FCC, N_A = 6.022 × 10<sup>23</sup>)
questions.explanation: d = (Z × M) / (a<sup>3</sup> × N_A) = (4 × 58.5) / ((5.64×10<sup>-8</sup>)<sup>3</sup> × 6.022×10<sup>23</sup>) ≈ 2160 kg/m<sup>3</sup> = 2.16 g/cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Packing efficiency of a simple cubic unit cell is approximately:
questions.explanation: Simple cubic packing efficiency = (π / 6) × 100% ≈ 52.4%.

questions.question: Coordination number of an atom in a Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) lattice is:
questions.explanation: In FCC / CCP structure, each sphere is in contact with 12 neighboring spheres.

questions.question: For a octahedral void, radius ratio r_cation / r_anion lies in the range:
questions.explanation: Octahedral void limiting radius ratio range is 0.414 to 0.732.

questions.question: Frenkel defect is a type of:
questions.explanation: Frenkel defect is a stoichiometric point defect where a smaller ion leaves its lattice site and occupies an interstitial position.

questions.question: In a BCC unit cell of edge length 'a', distance between two nearest neighboring atoms is:
questions.explanation: In BCC body diagonal = √3 a = 4 r. Nearest neighbor distance d = 2 r = √3 a / 2.

questions.question: Total volume occupied by spheres in a face-centered cubic (FCC) unit cell of radius r is:
questions.explanation: FCC has Z = 4 atoms. Total volume = 4 × (4/3 π r<sup>3</sup>) = (16/3) π r<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: A compound formed by elements A and B crystallizes in cubic structure where A atoms are at corners and B atoms at face centers. What is formula of compound?
questions.explanation: A = 8 × 1/8 = 1. B = 6 × 1/2 = 3. Empirical formula = AB3.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on Freundlich adsorption isotherm, colloidal particle charge, nuclear decay law, half-life, and binding energy.

questions.question: Half-life of a radioactive isotope is 10 hours. What percentage of original isotope remains after 30 hours?
questions.explanation: n = 30 / 10 = 3 half-lives. Fraction remaining = (1/2)<sup>3</sup> = 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5%.

questions.question: In Freundlich adsorption isotherm x/m = k P<sup>1/n</sup>, the value of 1/n lies between:
questions.explanation: The exponent 1/n ranges from 0 (high pressure independence) to 1 (low pressure linearity).

questions.question: Calculate binding energy per nucleon of Helium nucleus 4He2. (Mass of He = 4.0015 u, mass of proton = 1.0073 u, mass of neutron = 1.0087 u)
How many alpha (α) and beta (β⁻) particles are emitted during decay of 238U92 to 206Pb82?
questions.explanation: Mass change = 238 - 206 = 32. Number of α = 32 / 4 = 8. Atomic number change: 92 - (8×2) = 76. To reach 82, number of β emitted = 82 - 76 = 6.

questions.question: According to Hardy-Schulze rule, which ion has highest coagulating power for negatively charged As2S3 sol?
questions.explanation: Coagulating power increases rapidly with valency of active ion. For negative sol, Al³⁺ (+3 charge) is most effective.

questions.question: Decay constant λ of a radioactive sample is 0.0693 day<sup>-1</sup>. What is its mean life (τ)?
questions.explanation: Mean life τ = 1 / λ = 1 / 0.0693 ≈ 14.43 days.

questions.question: Coagulation value of an electrolyte for a sol is 5 mmol/L. How many mg of NaCl (Molar mass = 58.5) is required to coagulate 2 L of sol?
questions.explanation: For 2 L, millimoles required = 5 × 2 = 10 mmol = 0.01 mol. Mass = 0.01 × 58.5 g = 0.585 g = 585 mg.

questions.question: Gold number of gelatin is 0.005. How many mg of gelatin is required to prevent coagulation of 10 mL gold sol by 1 mL of 10% NaCl?
questions.explanation: By definition, Gold number is mass in mg of protective colloid required to prevent coagulation of 10 mL gold sol by 1 mL 10% NaCl. So mass = 0.005 mg.

questions.question: If 1 g of charcoal adsorbs 100 mL of 0.5 M CH3COOH to decrease concentration to 0.4 M, calculate mass of acetic acid adsorbed per gram of charcoal.
questions.explanation: Moles adsorbed = (0.5 - 0.4) × 0.1 L = 0.01 mol. Mass adsorbed = 0.01 × 60 g/mol = 0.6 g.

questions.question: A nuclear reactor produces 32 MW of power using 235U fission. If energy released per fission is 200 MeV, calculate number of fissions per second. (1 eV = 1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup> J)
questions.explanation: Energy per fission = 200 × 10<sup>6</sup> × 1.6×10<sup>-19</sup> J = 3.2 × 10<sup>-11</sup> J. Fissions per sec = (32 × 10<sup>6</sup> W) / (3.2 × 10<sup>-11</sup> J) = 1.0 × 10<sup>18</sup>.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on molarity, molality, normality, mole fraction, and dilution calculations.

questions.question: What volume of 10 M HCl must be diluted with water to prepare 2 Litres of 2 M HCl solution?
questions.explanation: Dilution equation: M1 V1 = M2 V2 => 10 × V1 = 2 × 2000 mL => 10 V1 = 4000 => V1 = 400 mL.

questions.question: Calculate the molality of a 20% (w/w) aqueous solution of KI. (Molar mass of KI = 166 g/mol)
questions.explanation: 20g KI in 80g water. Moles KI = 20 / 166 = 0.1205 mol. Mass solvent = 0.08 kg. Molality = 0.1205 / 0.08 ≈ 1.51 m.

questions.question: Find the mole fraction of ethanol (C2H5OH) in a mixture containing 46 g of ethanol and 54 g of water. (Molar mass: ethanol = 46, water = 18)
questions.explanation: Moles ethanol = 46 / 46 = 1 mol. Moles water = 54 / 18 = 3 mol. Mole fraction ethanol = 1 / (1 + 3) = 1/4 = 0.25.

questions.question: What is the molarity of pure water at 4°C? (Density of water = 1 g/mL)
questions.explanation: 1 L water = 1000 g = 1000 / 18 = 55.55 moles. Molarity = 55.55 mol / 1 L = 55.55 M.

questions.question: Equal volumes of 0.1 M HCl and 0.2 M NaOH are mixed. Calculate the resulting pH of the mixture.
Mass of Na2CO3 (Molar mass = 106 g/mol) required to prepare 250 mL of 0.1 M solution is:
questions.explanation: Moles = M × V(L) = 0.1 × 0.25 = 0.025. Mass = 0.025 × 106 = 2.65 g.

questions.question: Normality of a 30% (w/v) H2SO4 solution is: (Molar mass H2SO4 = 98 g/mol)
questions.explanation: 30% w/v = 300 g/L. Molarity = 300 / 98 ≈ 3.06 M. Normality = 3.06 × 2 = 6.12 N.

questions.question: Ppm (parts per million) concentration of a solution containing 2 mg of Ca<sup>2+</sup> ions in 1 kg of water is:
questions.explanation: ppm = (mass solute in mg) / (mass solution in kg) = 2 mg / 1 kg = 2 ppm.

questions.question: Calculate the volume strength of 1.5 N H2O2 solution.
questions.explanation: Volume strength = Normality × 5.6 = 1.5 × 5.6 = 8.4 V.

questions.question: Molarity of 10 Volume H2O2 solution is approximately:
questions.explanation: Molarity = Volume Strength / 5.6 = 10 / 5.6 ≈ 1.78 M.

quiz_sets.set_name: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure - Set 82
quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on bond dissociation energy, Hess's law, enthalpy of formation, and resonance energy.

questions.question: Calculate enthalpy change for H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2 HCl(g). Given Bond Energies: H-H = 435, Cl-Cl = 243, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol.
questions.explanation: ΔH = Σ BE(reactants) - Σ BE(products) = (435 + 243) - 2(431) = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ.

questions.question: Standard enthalpy of formation of liquid water is ΔHf = -285.8 kJ/mol. Calculate heat released when 36 g water is formed from H2 and O2.
questions.explanation: Moles of H2O = 36 / 18 = 2 moles. Heat released = 2 × 285.8 = 571.6 kJ.

questions.question: Enthalpy of combustion of C(s), H2(g), and C2H6(g) are -393.5, -285.8, and -1560.0 kJ/mol. Calculate ΔHf for C2H6(g).
Heat of atomization of methane CH4(g) is 1665 kJ/mol. What is the C-H average bond dissociation energy?
questions.explanation: CH4 contains 4 C-H bonds. Average bond energy = 1665 / 4 = 416.25 kJ/mol.

questions.question: Enthalpy of neutralization of strong acid (HCl) by strong base (NaOH) is -57.1 kJ/mol. Enthalpy of neutralization of HCN by NaOH is -12.1 kJ/mol. Calculate enthalpy of ionization of HCN.
questions.explanation: ΔH_neutralization = ΔH_ionization + ΔH_strong = ΔH_ion - 57.1 => -12.1 = ΔH_ion - 57.1 => ΔH_ion = +45.0 kJ/mol.

questions.question: Integral heat of solution of anhydrous CuSO4(s) is -66.5 kJ/mol and for CuSO4·5H2O(s) is +11.7 kJ/mol. Calculate heat of hydration of CuSO4(s).
questions.explanation: ΔH_hydration = ΔH1 - ΔH2 = -66.5 - (+11.7) = -78.2 kJ/mol.

questions.question: Resonance energy of Benzene is defined as the difference between:
options: Experimental heat of hydrogenation and calculated theoretical heat of hydrogenation
Heat of formation and heat of combustion
Bond energy of C-C and C=C
questions.explanation: Resonance energy = ΔH_hydrogenation(actual experimental) - ΔH_hydrogenation(theoretical for cyclohexatriene).

questions.question: For endothermic reaction A -> B, activation energy for forward reaction is 80 kJ/mol and ΔH = +30 kJ/mol. Calculate activation energy for reverse reaction.
questions.explanation: ΔH = Ea(forward) - Ea(reverse) => 30 = 80 - Ea(rev) => Ea(rev) = 80 - 30 = 50 kJ/mol.

questions.question: Heat of transition from graphite to diamond is +1.9 kJ/mol. Burning 12 g graphite produces -393.5 kJ. Burning 12 g diamond produces:
questions.explanation: C(graphite) -> C(diamond) ΔH = +1.9 kJ. Combustion C(diamond) = C(graphite) + (-1.9) = -393.5 - 1.9 = -395.4 kJ.

questions.question: Born-Haber cycle is used to determine:
questions.explanation: Born-Haber cycle uses Hess's law to calculate the lattice energy of ionic crystalline solids.

quiz_sets.set_name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids - Set 83
quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on colligative properties, van 't Hoff factor calculations, and abnormal molar masses.

questions.question: A 0.5% (w/v) solution of KCl (Molar mass = 74.5 g/mol) is 80% ionized. Calculate its van 't Hoff factor i.
questions.explanation: KCl -> K⁺ + Cl⁻ (n = 2). Degree of dissociation α = 0.80. i = 1 + (n - 1) α = 1 + (2 - 1) × 0.80 = 1.80.

questions.question: Acetic acid dimerizes in benzene to extent of 80%. Calculate the van 't Hoff factor i for acetic acid solution.
questions.explanation: 2 CH3COOH -> (CH3COOH)2. Association degree α = 0.80. i = 1 - α/2 = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60.

questions.question: Calculate depression in freezing point for 0.1 m aqueous solution of NaCl assuming complete dissociation. (Kf water = 1.86 K kg/mol)
questions.explanation: For NaCl i = 2. ΔTf = i × Kf × m = 2 × 1.86 × 0.1 = 0.372 K.

questions.question: Osmotic pressure of 0.1 M solution of non-electrolyte at 27°C (300 K) is: (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K)
questions.explanation: π = C × R × T = 0.1 × 0.0821 × 300 = 2.463 atm.

questions.question: Which of the following aqueous solutions will have the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: FeCl3 dissociates into 4 ions (Fe³⁺ + 3Cl⁻), giving largest van 't Hoff factor i = 4 and highest ΔTb.

questions.question: If experimental molar mass of Benzoic acid in benzene is 244 g/mol while theoretical mass is 122 g/mol, van 't Hoff factor i is:
questions.explanation: i = Normal Molar Mass / Observed Molar Mass = 122 / 244 = 0.5.

questions.question: Calculate freezing point of solution containing 62 g ethylene glycol (C2H6O2, Molar mass = 62) in 250 g water. (Kf = 1.86)
Hypertonic solution is one which has:
options: Higher osmotic pressure than reference solution
Lower osmotic pressure than reference solution
Same osmotic pressure as reference solution
questions.explanation: Hypertonic solution has a higher osmotic pressure relative to another solution.

questions.question: When red blood cells (RBCs) are placed in 0.9% (w/v) NaCl solution (isotonic), RBCs will:
questions.explanation: 0.9% NaCl solution is isotonic with blood plasma, so no net water movement occurs.

questions.question: Vapour pressure of solution containing 30 g non-volatile solute in 90 g water at 298 K is 2.8 kPa. VP of pure water is 3.0 kPa. Find molar mass of solute.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on conductivity, molar conductivity, Kohlrausch law, cell constant, and degree of dissociation.

questions.question: Molar conductivity at infinite dilution (Λ°m) for NaCl, HCl, and CH3COONa are 126.4, 425.9, and 91.0 S cm<sup>2</sup>/mol. Calculate Λ°m for CH3COOH.
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch Law: Λ°m(CH3COOH) = Λ°m(HCl) + Λ°m(CH3COONa) - Λ°m(NaCl) = 425.9 + 91.0 - 126.4 = 390.5 S cm<sup>2</sup>/mol.

questions.question: Conductivity of 0.001 M acetic acid is 4.95 × 10<sup>-5</sup> S cm<sup>-1</sup>. If Λ°m = 390.5 S cm<sup>2</sup>/mol, calculate degree of dissociation α.
Cell constant of a conductivity cell having electrode area A = 1.25 cm<sup>2</sup> separated by distance d = 0.5 cm is:
questions.explanation: Cell constant G = l / A = 0.5 cm / 1.25 cm<sup>2</sup> = 0.4 cm<sup>-1</sup>.

questions.question: SI unit of molar conductivity (Λm) is:
questions.explanation: SI unit of molar conductivity is Siemens meter square per mole (S m<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>).

questions.question: Resistance of 0.05 M NaOH solution cell is 200 Ω. If cell constant is 0.5 cm<sup>-1</sup>, calculate molar conductivity.
questions.explanation: Conductivity κ = cell constant / R = 0.5 / 200 = 0.0025 S cm<sup>-1</sup>. Λm = (0.0025 × 1000) / 0.05 = 2.5 / 0.05 = 50 S cm<sup>2</sup>/mol.

questions.question: Limiting molar conductivity of Mg<sup>2+</sup> is 106.0 S cm<sup>2</sup>/mol and for Cl<sup>-</sup> is 76.3 S cm<sup>2</sup>/mol. Calculate Λ°m for MgCl2.
On dilution, molar conductivity (Λm) of a weak electrolyte solution:
questions.explanation: On dilution degree of dissociation α increases rapidly towards 1, causing sharp increase in Λm.

questions.question: On dilution, specific conductivity (κ) of a solution:
questions.explanation: Specific conductivity decreases on dilution because number of ions per cm<sup>3</sup> of solution decreases.

questions.question: How much charge in Faradays is required to reduce 1 mole of Al<sup>3+</sup> to Al metal?
questions.explanation: Al<sup>3+</sup> + 3e<sup>-</sup> -> Al. 1 mole Al<sup>3+</sup> requires 3 moles of electrons = 3 Faraday.

questions.question: Standard reduction potentials: E°(Zn<sup>2+</sup>/Zn) = -0.76 V, E°(Fe<sup>2+</sup>/Fe) = -0.44 V. Standard EMF for cell Fe + Zn<sup>2+</sup> -> Fe<sup>2+</sup> + Zn is:
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°(Zn<sup>2+</sup>/Zn) - E°(Fe<sup>2+</sup>/Fe) = -0.76 - (-0.44) = -0.32 V (non-spontaneous).

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on photoelectric effect work function, threshold wavelength, Bohr energy levels, and hydrogen spectrum series.

questions.question: Threshold frequency for photoelectric emission of a metal is 1 × 10<sup>15</sup> Hz. Calculate its work function in eV. (h = 6.63 × 10<sup>-34</sup> J·s, 1 eV = 1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup> J)
questions.explanation: W = h × ν0 = 6.63 × 10<sup>-34</sup> × 10<sup>15</sup> = 6.63 × 10<sup>-19</sup> J = (6.63 × 10<sup>-19</sup>)/(1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup>) ≈ 4.14 eV.

questions.question: Calculate energy of photon having wavelength λ = 300 nm. (h c = 1240 eV·nm)
Radii of Bohr orbits in Hydrogen atom are proportional to:
questions.explanation: Bohr radius rn = 0.529 × n<sup>2</sup> Å ∝ n<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Velocity of electron in n-th Bohr orbit of H-atom is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Velocity vn = (2.18 × 10<sup>6</sup> × Z) / n m/s ∝ 1 / n.

questions.question: Wavelength of spectral line belonging to Balmer series of Hydrogen atom lies in which region?
questions.explanation: Balmer series transitions (n1 = 2) fall in the Visible light spectrum.

questions.question: Wave number of first line of Balmer series (n1 = 2, n2 = 3) in H-spectrum is: (R = Rydberg constant)
Maximum number of emission lines obtained when electron in n = 4 level of H-atom drops to ground state (n = 1) is:
questions.explanation: Number of lines = n (n - 1) / 2 = 4 × (4 - 1) / 2 = 12 / 2 = 6.

questions.question: De Broglie wavelength of an electron moving with 1% speed of light (3 × 10<sup>6</sup> m/s) is: (m = 9.1 × 10<sup>-31</sup> kg)
questions.explanation: λ = h / (m v) = (6.63 × 10<sup>-34</sup>) / (9.1 × 10<sup>-31</sup> × 3 × 10<sup>6</sup>) = 2.42 × 10<sup>-10</sup> m = 0.242 nm.

questions.question: If photon energy is E, momentum p of photon is:
questions.explanation: E = p × c => p = E / c.

questions.question: Potential energy of electron in 1st orbit of H-atom is: (Total energy E1 = -13.6 eV)
questions.explanation: In Bohr atom PE = 2 × Total E = 2 × (-13.6) = -27.2 eV.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on real gas deviation, compressibility factor Z, liquefaction of gases, and inversion temperature.

questions.question: For a real gas at high pressure, van der Waals equation simplifies to (neglecting 'a'):
questions.explanation: At high pressure P >> a/V<sup>2</sup>, so equation becomes P (V - b) = RT => Z = 1 + Pb/RT > 1.

questions.question: At low pressure, van der Waals equation simplifies to (neglecting 'b'):
questions.explanation: (P + a/V<sup>2</sup>) V = RT => PV + a/V = RT => Z = PV/RT = 1 - a/(V RT) < 1.

questions.question: Inversion temperature (T_i) of a gas is related to van der Waals constants by:
questions.explanation: Inversion temperature T_i = 2a / (R b) = 2 T_B.

questions.question: Critical volume (V_c) of 1 mole of a van der Waals gas is equal to:
questions.explanation: Critical volume V_c = 3b.

questions.question: Critical pressure (P_c) of a van der Waals gas is given by:
questions.explanation: Critical pressure P_c = a / (27 b<sup>2</sup>).

questions.question: Ease of liquefaction of a gas increases with:
options: Higher value of van der Waals constant 'a'
Lower value of van der Waals constant 'a'
questions.explanation: Larger 'a' value indicates stronger intermolecular attractive forces, making liquefaction easier.

questions.question: Which of the following gases exhibits Z > 1 at all pressures at room temperature?
questions.explanation: H2 and He have extremely weak attractive forces ('a' is negligible), so Z = 1 + Pb/RT > 1 at all pressures.

questions.question: Ratio of critical temperature T_c to Boyle's temperature T_B for a gas is:
questions.explanation: T_c = 8a / (27 Rb) and T_B = a / (Rb). Ratio T_c / T_B = (8/27 Rb) / (1/Rb) = 8 / 27.

questions.question: Density of gas X is twice that of gas Y at same T and P. Ratio of molar mass MX : MY is:
questions.explanation: P M = d R T => M ∝ d. Since dX = 2 dY, MX : MY = 2 : 1.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on buffer capacity, salt hydrolysis, solubility product, and common ion effect.

questions.question: Calculate pH of 0.1 M NH4Cl aqueous solution. (Kb of NH4OH = 1.8 × 10<sup>-5</sup>, Kw = 10<sup>-14</sup>)
questions.explanation: Salt of weak base + strong acid: pH = 0.5 [ pKw - pKb - log C ] = 0.5 [ 14 - 4.74 - (-1) ] = 0.5 [ 10.26 ] = 5.13.

questions.question: Calculate pH of 0.1 M CH3COONa aqueous solution. (Ka of CH3COOH = 1.8 × 10<sup>-5</sup>)
questions.explanation: Salt of weak acid + strong base: pH = 0.5 [ pKw + pKa + log C ] = 0.5 [ 14 + 4.74 + (-1) ] = 0.5 [ 17.74 ] = 8.87.

questions.question: Hydrolysis constant Kh for salt of weak acid and weak base (e.g. CH3COONH4) is given by:
questions.explanation: For salt of weak acid + weak base: Kh = Kw / (Ka × Kb).

questions.question: pH of salt of weak acid and weak base is independent of:
questions.explanation: Formula: pH = 7 + 0.5 (pKa - pKb), which is completely independent of concentration C.

questions.question: Calculate solubility of AgCl in 0.1 M NaCl solution. (Ksp AgCl = 1 × 10<sup>-10</sup>)
questions.explanation: Common ion [Cl⁻] = 0.1 M. Ksp = [Ag⁺] [Cl⁻] => 10<sup>-10</sup> = s × 0.1 => s = 10<sup>-9</sup> M.

questions.question: Maximum buffer capacity of an acidic buffer occurs when ratio of [Salt] / [Acid] is:
questions.explanation: Buffer capacity is maximum when [Salt] = [Acid], i.e., pH = pKa.

questions.question: Which of the following mixtures acts as a basic buffer solution?
questions.explanation: A basic buffer consists of a weak base (NH4OH) and its salt with a strong acid (NH4Cl).

questions.question: Solubility product of PbI2 is Ksp = 3.2 × 10<sup>-8</sup>. Calculate its molar solubility in pure water.
questions.explanation: PbI2 <=> Pb<sup>2+</sup> + 2 I<sup>-</sup>. Ksp = s × (2s)<sup>2</sup> = 4 s<sup>3</sup> => 4 s<sup>3</sup> = 3.2 × 10<sup>-8</sup> => s<sup>3</sup> = 8 × 10<sup>-9</sup> => s = 2 × 10<sup>-3</sup> M.

questions.question: On adding 0.01 mole of NaOH to 1 Litre of buffer solution, its pH changes from 4.74 to 4.76. Buffer capacity is:
questions.explanation: Buffer capacity = moles of acid/base added / pH change = 0.01 / (4.76 - 4.74) = 0.01 / 0.02 = 0.5.

questions.question: Precipitation of an ionic salt occurs when ionic product (Qsp) is:
questions.explanation: Precipitation occurs only when ionic product Qsp > Ksp (supersaturated solution).

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on redox titrations, dichromate/permanganate titrations, and iodometry.

questions.question: How many moles of K2Cr2O7 are required to completely oxidize 6 moles of FeSO4 in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: Cr2O7<sup>2-</sup> + 14 H<sup>+</sup> + 6 Fe<sup>2+</sup> -> 2 Cr<sup>3+</sup> + 6 Fe<sup>3+</sup> + 7 H2O. 1 mole K2Cr2O7 oxidizes 6 moles Fe<sup>2+</sup>.

questions.question: How many moles of KMnO4 are required to oxidize 5 moles of oxalic acid (H2C2O4) in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: 2 MnO4<sup>-</sup> + 5 C2O4<sup>2-</sup> + 16 H<sup>+</sup> -> 2 Mn<sup>2+</sup> + 10 CO2 + 8 H2O. 2 moles KMnO4 oxidize 5 moles oxalic acid.

questions.question: In iodometric titration, equivalent weight of Na2S2O3·5H2O (Molar mass = M) is:
questions.explanation: Reaction: 2 S2O3<sup>2-</sup> + I2 -> S4O6<sup>2-</sup> + 2 I<sup>-</sup>. Oxidation state change of S per mole of Na2S2O3 is 1. Eq mass = M / 1.

questions.question: Find n-factor of FeSO4 in reaction: FeSO4 -> Fe2(SO4)3.
questions.explanation: Fe changes from +2 to +3. Change in oxidation number per Fe atom = 1. So n-factor = 1.

questions.question: Find n-factor of FeC2O4 (Ferrous Oxalate) when completely oxidized to Fe<sup>3+</sup> and CO2.
questions.explanation: Fe<sup>2+</sup> -> Fe<sup>3+</sup> (1 e<sup>-</sup>) and C2O4<sup>2-</sup> -> 2 CO2 (2 e<sup>-</sup>). Total electrons lost per mole = 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.question: What volume of 0.2 M KMnO4 is required to oxidize 50 mL of 0.5 M H2O2 in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: n-factor KMnO4 = 5, n-factor H2O2 = 2. N1 V1 = N2 V2 => (0.2 × 5) × V1 = (0.5 × 2) × 50 => 1.0 V1 = 1.0 × 50 => wait, 1.0 V1 = 20 mL.

questions.question: Oxidation state of Nitrogen in NH4NO3 (Ammonium nitrate) is:
questions.explanation: In NH4<sup>+</sup> nitrogen is -3. In NO3<sup>-</sup> nitrogen is +5.

questions.question: Oxidation number of Iron in Fe3O4 (Magnetite) is average oxidation state equal to:
questions.explanation: Fe3O4 is mixed oxide FeO·Fe2O3. Total charge 3x + 4(-2) = 0 => 3x = 8 => x = +8/3.

questions.question: Oxidation state of Sulfur in Caro's acid (H2SO5) is:
questions.explanation: H2SO5 contains one peroxide linkage (-O-O-). H2 S O3(O2): 2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 => 2 + x - 6 - 2 = 0 => x = +6.

questions.question: Disproportionation reaction is one in which:
options: Same element is simultaneously oxidized and reduced
questions.explanation: In a disproportionation reaction, the same species undergoes both oxidation and reduction.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on Bragg's law, Schottky defect, Frenkel defect, and crystal lattice density.

questions.question: Bragg's law for X-ray diffraction from crystal planes is expressed as:
questions.explanation: Bragg's Law: n λ = 2 d sinθ.

questions.question: First order diffraction (n = 1) of X-rays of wavelength 1.54 Å from crystal plane occurs at angle θ = 30°. Find interplanar distance d.
Schottky defect in ionic solids leads to:
questions.explanation: Schottky defect creates equal cation and anion vacancies, reducing total mass without changing volume, so density decreases.

questions.question: Frenkel defect does not change the density of crystal because:
options: Equal number of ions leave crystal
questions.explanation: In Frenkel defect, ions simply displace to interstitial sites inside the crystal, so mass and volume remain constant.

questions.question: F-centers in alkali halide crystals (e.g. NaCl yellow color) are:
options: Anion vacancies occupied by unpaired electrons
questions.explanation: F-centers (Farbezenter / color centers) are anionic vacancies trapped by unpaired electrons.

questions.question: Radius ratio r+ / r- for CsCl (cubic structure, CN = 8) lies in range:
questions.explanation: For 8-coordinated cubic structure (like CsCl), radius ratio range is 0.732 to 1.000.

questions.question: Edge length of face-centered cubic cell of ionic solid AB is 508 pm. If radius of anion B- is 144 pm, radius of cation A+ is:
questions.explanation: For NaCl-type FCC lattice: 2 (r+ + r-) = a => r+ + 144 = 508 / 2 = 254 => r+ = 254 - 144 = 110 pm.

questions.question: Percentage of empty space in Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) unit cell is:
questions.explanation: Packing efficiency of BCC is 68%. Void space / empty space = 100 - 68 = 32%.

questions.question: Ferromagnetic substance turns paramagnetic above temperature called:
questions.explanation: At Curie temperature (Tc), domain structure breaks down and ferromagnetic substance becomes paramagnetic.

questions.question: Doping of Silicon with Group 15 element (e.g. Phosphorus) produces:
questions.explanation: Group 15 element introduces extra free electrons, creating an n-type (negative carrier) semiconductor.

quiz_sets.set_description: 10 Chapterwise numerical problems on radioactive decay series, binding energy, half-life, average life, and nuclear reaction energy.

questions.question: Calculate energy released in fission of 1 g of 235U if 200 MeV is released per fission. (N_A = 6.022 × 10<sup>23</sup>)
questions.explanation: Fissions = (1/235) × 6.022×10<sup>23</sup> = 2.56×10<sup>21</sup>. E = 2.56×10<sup>21</sup> × 200 × 1.6×10<sup>-13</sup> J ≈ 8.2 × 10<sup>10</sup> J.

questions.question: Radioactive element has half-life of 1600 years. Calculate its decay constant λ.
Activity of a radioactive sample drops to 1/16 of its initial value in 80 minutes. Calculate half-life of sample.
questions.explanation: (1/2)<sup>n</sup> = 1/16 = (1/2)<sup>4</sup> => n = 4 half-lives. t1/2 = 80 / 4 = 20 minutes.

questions.question: Unit of radioactivity 'Curie' (Ci) is defined as:
questions.explanation: 1 Curie (Ci) = 3.7 × 10<sup>10</sup> dps (disintegrations per second).

questions.question: 1 Becquerel (Bq) is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 Bq = 1 disintegration per second (SI unit of radioactivity).

questions.question: In nuclear fusion reaction 2H1 + 3H1 -> 4He2 + 1n0, energy released is due to:
questions.explanation: In nuclear fusion, total mass of products is less than reactants; mass defect Δm is converted to energy via E = Δm c<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Alpha (α) decay of a nucleus reduces mass number A and atomic number Z respectively by:
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is 4He2 nucleus, so A decreases by 4 and Z decreases by 2.

questions.question: Beta negative (β⁻) decay increases atomic number Z by:
questions.explanation: In β⁻ decay a neutron converts to a proton: n -> p + e⁻ + ν_bar, so Z increases by 1 while A remains unchanged.

questions.question: Gamma (γ) radiation emitted by radioactive nucleus consists of:
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy, uncharged electromagnetic photons.

questions.question: A radioactive sample has 10<sup>20</sup> active nuclei. If half-life is 100 s, find initial activity of sample.
questions.explanation: Activity A = λ × N = (0.693 / 100) × 10<sup>20</sup> = 6.93 × 10<sup>17</sup> Bq.
